parts.t: Polymer banknotes: features and global experience
items: **Material:** Polymer banknotes are made from a non-fibrous, non-porous plastic film.
**Existing paper notes:** Existing Indian paper banknotes use long cotton fibres from cotton comber and cotton linter.
**Circulation:** Polymer notes are proposed to circulate alongside existing ₹10 and ₹20 paper notes.
**Legal tender:** Existing paper notes will remain legal tender.
**Trials will assess:** cleanliness, security, handling and suitability for India's cash economy.
**Australia** first issued a polymer banknote in **1988**.
**More than 60 countries** reportedly use polymer currency.
**Examples:** Canada, United Kingdom, New Zealand and Singapore.

parts.t: Digital Rupee: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)
items: **Digital Rupee** is also known as **e₹** or **e-rupee**.
**Nature:** It is a tokenised digital form of the Indian rupee.
**Issuer:** Issued by the Reserve Bank of India.
**Status:** It is India's Central Bank Digital Currency.

parts.t: Five-nation tour of May 2026: UAE, Norway and Italy
items: **Five-nation tour:** The UAE was the first country in a five-nation tour, followed by the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway and Italy.
**IMEC:** India and UAE reaffirmed the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), launched at the 2023 G20 Summit.
**LNG:** HPCL and ADNOC Gas signed a ten-year agreement for 0.5 million metric tonnes per annum of LNG from 2028.
**Culture:** Proposed a House of India museum in Abu Dhabi and UAE artefacts for Lothal's National Maritime Heritage Complex.
**Dialogue:** It includes a section on the first Maritime Security, Disarmament and Non-Proliferation Dialogue in Oslo.
**Visit:** 19–20 May 2026. Met Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and President Sergio Mattarella.
At FAO headquarters in Rome, Modi received the **Agricola Medal**, the FAO's highest honour, awarded for contributions to food security, sustainable agriculture and rural development.
**Year of Culture and Tourism:** India and Italy designated 2027 as the Year of Culture and Tourism.
**Cooperation** included defence, counterterrorism, space, technology and IMEC.
**Trade target:** India–Italy bilateral trade target of €20 billion by 2029.
**State visit:** Prime Minister's state visit on 27–29 June 2026.
**Talks:** Held talks with President Dr Patrick Herminie.
**Coincided with:** the 50th anniversary of Seychelles' independence and the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties with India.
**Second visit:** It was Modi's second visit after March 2015.
**Joint Vision:** Advanced the February 2026 Joint Vision.
**Cooperation:** Expanded cooperation between the two countries.
**Summit:** Third Australia–India Annual Summit held in Melbourne on 9 July.
**Invitation** extended by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
**Partnership:** Advanced the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership established in 2020.
**Security:** Expanded 2009 security framework; Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap.
**Maritime cooperation:** Maritime-domain awareness and surveillance; information exchange and operational coordination; search and rescue and sea-lane protection.
**MoU** between Indian Coast Guard and Australia's Maritime Border Command.
**Uranium:** Cooperation on peaceful uranium exports under IAEA safeguards.
**Support:** Australia's support for India's NSG membership and Gaganyaan programme.

lectures.title: President Droupadi Murmu: visits, events, Padma Awards 2026 and appointments

items: **Countries visited:** Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania.
First visit by an Indian President to **Moldova** and to **North Macedonia**; first visit to **Romania** since President Shankar Dayal Sharma's visit in May 1994.
**Host:** Maia Sandu. President Murmu met President Maia Sandu and parliamentary leaders.
**Key areas of cooperation:** agriculture; healthcare and pharmaceuticals; renewable energy; Digital Public Infrastructure; Artificial Intelligence; infrastructure connectivity.
**Important project reference:** KEC International's 400-kV Vulcănesti–Chişinău transmission line illustrated India's infrastructure involvement.
**Moldova's strategic significance:** links to European value chains; access to the Black Sea region.
**Host:** Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova. President Murmu met the President and addressed the Assembly.
**First:** This was the first-ever visit by an Indian President to North Macedonia.
**Emphasised** democratic values, parliamentary diplomacy and peace.
**Trade:** Both sides aimed to double bilateral trade by the end of the decade.
**Pharmaceuticals:** Proposed joint pharmaceutical manufacturing for Balkan and European markets.
**Healthcare:** Healthcare cooperation MoU renewed for five years, including traditional medicine.
**Mother Teresa Memorial:** Visited the Mother Teresa Memorial.
**Trade:** India and Romania agreed to work towards doubling bilateral trade over the next three years.
**India–EU FTA:** The India–EU Free Trade Agreement concluded in January 2026 was viewed as an opportunity for deeper economic ties.
**Defence:** Both countries sought stronger defence cooperation through training, industrial contacts, possible joint production and co-development.
**Three documents were signed**, including the Science and Technology Programme for 2026–2029 and Memoranda of Understanding and related cooperation arrangements.
